A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VM/FVM research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–G are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching the renumbered appendix tables.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on mislabeled-sample detection, relabeling, and influential-sample identification in text and image generation, plus ablations and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experimental outcomes in Tables 1–6 and appendix Tables 7–10.

M1.justification: The VM/FVM objectives, validation tuning, influence estimators, diagonal Fisher approximation, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The inverse-Hessian alternatives in Appendix C.4 are also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same CIFAR noisy-label tasks, sentence transformations, math problems with reasoning, and image style/subject tasks. Removing their template descriptions does not establish a change in evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within the main experiments and appendix comparisons. In particular, the EK-FAC/EK-FAC* comparison in v2 Table 10 remains in v3 Table 7.

E3.justification: The splits, metrics, model configurations, and training/tuning settings are retained. Appendix B.3 specifies 50 validation pairs per style, 150 total, in both versions; deleting v2 Table 9 removes a conflicting 150-per-style caption without establishing a changed experimental setting.

E4.justification: The component ablation in Section 4.5 and the validation-size, sharpness-aware optimizer, and inverse-Hessian analyses in Appendix C.2–C.4 are unchanged. Their supporting results are retained under renumbered tables.

E5.justification: Three-run mean and standard-deviation reporting is retained for the corresponding classification and appendix comparisons. Generation metrics still summarize variation across validation samples; no run counts or uncertainty procedures change.

E6.justification: The reported numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged. v2 Tables 10–13 match v3 Tables 7–10; the deleted Tables 7–9 contain task templates, not measured experimental outcomes.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1, Theorem 3.2, Corollary 3.3, and the proofs and derivations in Appendices D–E are unchanged. Their different page positions reflect appendix reflow.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about validation-risk sharpness, influence-estimation error, the proposed estimator, and empirical superiority.

C2.justification: The interpretations and qualifications are unchanged, including the LPF hyperparameter explanation for FVM not always outperforming VM and the discussion of inverse-Hessian approximation sensitivity in Appendix C.4.

D1.justification: v2 Tables 7–9 are removed, including ten sentence-transformation examples and ten math prompts with reasoning templates. Appendix B.2–B.3 instead directs readers to Kwon et al. (2024). The general image-prompt format, implementation settings, and code-access statement remain.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work discussion are unchanged. Kwon et al. (2024) was already credited for the removed templates; the replacement pointers introduce no new cited work or research positioning.

P1.justification: Three sentences in Appendix B.2–B.3 replace internal table references with pointers to Kwon et al. (2024), alongside a punctuation edit and updated table references. The main narrative and section hierarchy remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Three descriptive template tables are deleted. The remaining appendix tables are renumbered and repositioned as surrounding material reflows, while retaining their structure. Figures 1–3 and main Tables 1–6 are visually unchanged.

improvement.justification: Removing v2 Tables 7–8 makes the text-task specifications less transparent and less self-contained, with v3 directing readers elsewhere for the transformations and math templates. Deleting the largely redundant image-template table also removes its conflicting sample-count caption, but this limited benefit does not outweigh the lost text-task detail. Methods, theory, and empirical support remain unchanged.
